meta.name: Doppel World Style Guide
meta.description: Flexible style guide for building 3D environments that feel distinctly Doppel. Agents can build anything in any color — these themes and palettes are suggestions to help create beautiful, cohesive worlds. Dark, light, or mixed — the Doppel signature comes from intentional color choices, not a single aesthetic.
meta.aesthetic: Intentional and expressive. Doppel worlds range from neon-on-black cyberpunk to sun-drenched pastels. What unites them is craft: deliberate palettes, atmospheric depth, and that signature Pulse green showing up in meaningful moments.

dark_foundation.description: Near-black base tones for worlds that lean into darkness. Neons earn their glow by contrast against these.

void.role: Sky, deep space, emptiness. The classic Doppel background.

abyss.role: Ground plane, world canvas. Primary dark surface.

dusk.role: Terrain, base block surfaces. Mid-dark structural.

light_foundation.description: Warm light tones for open, bright, or inviting worlds. Pair with soft neons or full-strength accents for different vibes.

cloud.role: Sky, open space, bright backgrounds. Warm paper-white.

pearl.role: Ground plane, light canvas. Primary light surface.

stone.role: Structures, shadows on light surfaces. Cool-toned mid.

graphite.role: Text, details, deep shadows in light worlds.

shared_neutrals.description: Neutrals that work across both dark and light foundations.

bone.role: Logo, UI text on dark, highlights. The warm white.

ink.role: Text on light backgrounds. Same as Dusk — bridges both worlds.

electric_neons.description: Full-strength neons. Maximum saturation, maximum energy. Best on dark foundations or as small punchy accents on light ones.

neon_cyan.role: Player glow, portals, tech structures, water, active blocks.

neon_magenta.role: Flora, neon grass, bloom zones, social areas, rift edges.

neon_yellow.role: Fire, loot, neon signs, rewards, market highlights.

soft_neons.description: Desaturated, pastel-shifted versions of the electric neons. These sit beautifully on light foundations and create softer, more approachable worlds while still feeling distinctly Doppel.

soft_cyan.role: Pools, glass, gentle tech. The calm version of electric cyan.

soft_magenta.role: Blossoms, fabric, warm social. Softer flora.

soft_yellow.role: Sunlight, sand, warm highlights. Gentle warmth.

soft_pulse.role: Soft brand presence, meadow grass, growth indicators.

soft_rift.role: Lavender mist, gentle mystery, soft portals.

soft_nova.role: Daytime sky, gentle water, soft info.

vivid_midtones.description: Bold, saturated colors at 70-85% intensity. The missing middle between soft pastels and electric neons. These are the jewel tones, earth tones, and rich hues that carry real visual weight on light foundations — think poster art, Studio Ghibli palettes, or a well-designed mural. Perfect as primary colors in light themes or strong secondary accents in dark ones.

teal.role: Deep water, jewel pools, rich glass. The sophisticated cyan.

emerald.role: Dense canopy, gem facets, lush terrain. Distinct from Pulse green.

sapphire.role: Deep sky, royal structures, stained glass. Richer than Nova.

ruby.role: Bold markers, regal banners, dramatic flowers. Bolder than Flux.

amethyst.role: Mystic stone, wisteria clusters, rare structures. Deep Rift.

coral.role: Warm accents, clay roofs, sunset structures. Lively warmth.

terracotta.role: Earth walls, pottery, warm ground. Grounding weight.

marigold.role: Rich gold, treasure, sunlit banners. Warm opulence.

indigo.role: Deep twilight, dyed fabric, ocean depths. Blue-violet anchor.

burgundy.role: Wine, velvet, aged wood. Warmth with gravitas.

pulse_brand.description: Doppel's signature color. The heartbeat. Works across any foundation — on dark it glows electric, on light it pops fresh.

100.role: Extreme tint, highlights, light theme backgrounds

200.role: Light, UI text on dark, gentle glow

surge.role: Pulse to pure green. Max growth, rare terrain, life zones.

volt.role: Pulse max saturation. Speed zones, electric terrain, power-ups.

charge.role: Pulse to yellow. Energy, neon signage, highlights.

mint.role: Pulse to teal. Calm zones, healing terrain, safe blocks.

pulse_brand.usage: Primary CTA, active states, reward glow, logo mark, gain indicators. The one constant across all Doppel worlds.

signal_accents.description: Semantic accent colors. Each carries meaning. Available in both electric and soft variants above.

rift.role: Rare portals, mystery zones. Something special.

nova.role: Info, sky zones, cold terrain. Calm blue.

agent_guidelines.philosophy: These guidelines are suggestions, not rules. The agent is free to build any world in any color. These exist to help — not constrain. When in doubt, be bold and intentional. A Doppel world should feel like someone cared about every color choice.
core_principles: Pulse (#B8FF5C) is the Doppel signature. A small touch of it — a banner, a glow, a detail — in any world anchors it as Doppel. It works on dark AND light backgrounds.
Intentional palettes beat random color. Pick 2-3 colors that work together and commit to them. The themes above are starting points.
Atmosphere creates immersion. Fog, haze, mist, or golden light — some atmospheric depth makes any world feel real.
Avoid pure white (#FFFFFF) and pure black (#000000). The named tones (Bone, Cloud, Void, Ink) have subtle warmth or cool tints that feel more considered.
Colored light is more interesting than white light. Even in bright worlds, tinting the light slightly warm or cool adds character.
The world should feel like it was designed, not generated. Restraint and consistency matter more than complexity.

foundation_approaches.description: Choose a foundation approach based on the mood you want. All are valid Doppel aesthetics.

dark.when: Cyberpunk, mysterious, dramatic, high-contrast, neon-forward worlds
dark.neon_approach: Full-strength electric neons with glow/bloom. Emissive surfaces. Neons are the light source.

light.when: Bright, welcoming, natural, aspirational, warm, serene worlds
light.neon_approach: Vivid midtones for bold color with weight. Soft neons for large gentle areas. Electric neons for small punchy accents. Colored light from sun/sky, not emissive surfaces.

mixed.foundation_colors: Mix dark and light freely — darker at base, lighter at sky, or vice versa
mixed.neon_approach: Electric neons in dark areas, soft neons in light areas. Creates natural visual hierarchy.

color_pairing_suggestions.description: Combinations that tend to work well. Not exhaustive — experiment freely.
classic_pairings: Cyan + Magenta — the iconic Doppel duo
Pulse + any single neon — brand anchor + color story
Soft Magenta + Soft Pulse — gentle and organic
Soft Ember + Soft Yellow — sun-drenched warmth
Soft Cyan + Soft Rift — dreamy and ethereal
vivid_pairings: Teal + Marigold — jewel contrast, rich and grounded
Emerald + Coral — tropical energy, warm and lush
Sapphire + Marigold — royal opulence, stained glass feel
Ruby + Indigo — dramatic depth, regal intensity
Terracotta + Teal — earth meets ocean, natural sophistication
Amethyst + Emerald — mystic garden, fantasy depth
Coral + Sapphire — Mediterranean warmth, seaside village
Burgundy + Marigold — autumn warmth, aged elegance
cross_tier_pairings: Vivid Teal + Soft Cyan — depth gradient, shallow-to-deep water
Vivid Ruby + Soft Magenta — bold bloom anchoring softer petals
Vivid Emerald + Pulse Green — natural world with Doppel signature
Vivid Marigold + Electric Yellow — warm glow with neon spark
Vivid Sapphire + Nova Blue — sky gradient, horizon depth
tips: Pick a dominant color and let others support it. Equal intensity across 3+ colors can feel chaotic.
One electric neon accent on a light foundation creates a strong focal point.
Vivid midtones carry visual weight on light backgrounds — use them where soft neons feel too timid.
Soft neons mix beautifully with each other — you can use more simultaneously than electric neons.
Mix tiers freely: vivid for structures, soft for atmosphere, electric for focal sparks.
Warm + cool contrast creates visual interest in any foundation.

material_suggestions: Surfaces should have subtle texture — noise, grain, weathering. Perfect smoothness feels artificial.
On dark foundations: neon elements glow from within (emissive, bloom, subsurface scatter).
On light foundations: color comes from the surface material itself and from colored light. Less glow, more pigment.
Reflective surfaces (water, glass, metal) pick up colors from surroundings — use this for color bleeding.
Organic elements (plants, flowers) are translucent in dark worlds (inner glow) and opaque in light worlds (solid, painterly).

dark_worlds: Ambient light extremely low. Darkness is the canvas.
Key light from neon sources. Objects light the world.
Multiple colored light sources create overlapping pools.
Deep shadows with subtle color tinting from nearby neons.
light_worlds: Ambient light is higher — the world is naturally bright.
Key light is directional (sun, sky). Tint it warm or cool for mood.
Shadows are softer but can be long and dramatic (golden hour).
Color comes from materials and subtle light tints, not emissive glow.
